Resource Directory

The following resources are organized by category. All links were current at the time of course publication. Verify currency before operational use. No endorsement of commercial products is implied.

Paid Blockchain Forensics & Intelligence Platforms

  • Chainalysis Reactor — Industry standard for law enforcement. Visual transaction graphing, entity attribution, and case management integration.
  • TRM Labs — Cross-chain tracing covering DeFi protocols and bridge hops.
  • Elliptic — Regulatory compliance focus; VASP exposure analysis.
  • Global Ledger — High-risk entity identification and visual graph analysis.
  • Merkle Science — Predictive risk scoring and DeFi protocol analysis.
  • Breadcrumbs — Affordable visualization tool with free and paid tiers. Useful for initial triage.

Free OSINT Tools

  • Mempool.space — Best Bitcoin network visualizer. Shows real-time fees and unconfirmed transaction status.
  • Bitquery — Graph-based tool for Ethereum and EVM-compatible chains. Limited free tier.
  • MistTrack — Compliance-focused address risk lookups. Free tier available.
  • MetaSleuth — Visual graph tracing for Ethereum and Layer-2 networks.
  • Orbit — Open-source Python-based blockchain crawler for technical analysts.
  • WalletExplorer — Legacy Bitcoin wallet clustering tool.

Blockchain Explorers

  • Bitcoin: Blockchain.com Explorer, Blockchair
  • Ethereum / EVM: Etherscan.io, Polygonscan, Arbiscan
  • Tron: Tronscan
  • Solana: Solscan

Federal Reporting

  • IC3.gov — FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center. Primary intake for cyber-enabled fraud and cryptocurrency crimes.
  • FinCEN MSB Registrant Search — Verify Bitcoin ATM operators as registered Money Services Businesses.
  • FTC Fraud Report — Federal Trade Commission consumer fraud intake. Used for federal enforcement prioritization.

LE Working Groups

  • NW3C (National White Collar Crime Center) — Free training and technical support for state and local law enforcement agencies.
  • REACT Task Force — Model for multi-agency cyber and financial crimes task forces.
  • GASO (Global Anti-Scam Organization) — Pig Butchering victim support network and criminal intelligence resource.
  • Genesis Digital Assets Academy — Comprehensive law enforcement cryptocurrency training.
  • Deconflict — Case and address deconfliction across agencies.

Industry Partners — Law Enforcement Portals

  • Tether (USDT) Law Enforcement Portal — Submit freeze requests for USDT wallets.
  • Circle (USDC) Law Enforcement Compliance — Submit freeze requests for USDC wallets.
  • Coinbase Law Enforcement Portal — Preservation letters, subpoenas, and emergency requests.
  • Binance Law Enforcement Request System — Formal LE request submission for account and transaction records.

questions.q: An officer encounters a wallet address beginning with the letter T on a suspect's phone. Which blockchain and asset type is this most likely associated with?
options: Bitcoin on the Lightning Network.
Ethereum tokens on the Polygon sidechain.
A Bitcoin SegWit address — all SegWit addresses start with T.
USDT or TRX on the Tron blockchain, a network frequently used for low-cost cartel money transfers and Pig Butchering payments.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Bitcoin from USDT (Tether) as a tool for criminal financial activity?
options: Bitcoin can be frozen by the US Treasury; USDT cannot.
USDT maintains a stable $1.00 value and can be frozen by Tether Ltd. on a valid LE request; Bitcoin cannot be frozen by any central authority.
Bitcoin is untraceable on the blockchain; USDT transactions are fully public.
USDT is exclusively used on the Bitcoin blockchain; BTC is used on Ethereum.

questions.q: A suspect's Ethereum wallet shows a balance of $30 in ETH. The officer concludes the wallet is low-value and does not document the token holdings. What investigative error occurred?
options: ETH wallets with under $100 do not require documentation under FinCEN thresholds.
The officer failed to examine ERC-20 token holdings — the same address may contain millions in USDT or other tokens that are separate from the ETH balance.
Ethereum tokens require a separate warrant from the ETH balance and should not be examined without one.
No error occurred — the ETH balance is the only relevant figure for a criminal investigation.

questions.q: A MetaMask app is found on a suspect's phone. The suspect claims ignorance. Which fact most directly undermines the claim of unknowing installation?
options: Non-custodial wallets require the user to manually write down and re-enter a 12-word seed phrase to complete setup — a deliberate, multi-step process that cannot be completed accidentally.
MetaMask is sold in Apple and Google app stores, making it widely accessible.
MetaMask uses biometric login that ties the account to the device owner.
Custodial wallets like Coinbase require ID upload, which would prove the suspect's identity.

questions.q: During a vehicle search, an officer finds a crumpled receipt from a gas station kiosk and $8,500 in banded cash. The most likely criminal activity indicated by this combination is:
options: A legitimate cryptocurrency investor diversifying into cash holdings.
A drug transaction where cash was the payment method.
A smurfing operation using a money mule to structure Bitcoin ATM deposits below reporting thresholds.
A ransomware victim who withdrew cash to pay a Bitcoin ATM ransom.

questions.q: A victim was directed to connect her crypto wallet to a website, after which all her funds disappeared in a single transaction she did not authorize. This describes which attack method?
options: A SIM-swap attack targeting the victim's phone carrier.
A Bitcoin mixer that intercepted the victim's transaction in the mempool.
A remote wipe command issued to the victim's hardware wallet.
A wallet drainer — a malicious smart contract that was authorized when the victim connected her wallet, granting the suspect permission to drain funds without further approval.

questions.q: A Pig Butchering victim's funds were confirmed in a USDT wallet 18 hours ago. Which action has the highest probability of fund recovery at this moment?
options: Issue a local arrest warrant for the overseas suspects.
File an IC3 report and await federal guidance.
Contact Tether's law enforcement compliance portal immediately to request a wallet freeze.
Subpoena the Ethereum blockchain for subscriber records.

questions.q: A police report states: "Victim lost $15,000 in crypto last week." A financial crimes detective says this report is unsolvable. Which element, if added, would most directly enable a blockchain trace?
options: The victim's date of birth.
The name of the crypto exchange the victim used.
The Transaction Hash (TxID) — the unique digital fingerprint of the specific transfer on the blockchain.
The IP address of the scam website the victim visited.

questions.q: An officer seizes an unlocked phone showing an active crypto wallet during an arrest. The correct immediate sequence is:
options: Power off the phone to preserve the current state, then bag it.
Allow the suspect to lock the phone themselves to maintain chain of custody.
Enable Airplane Mode, place the device in a Faraday Bag, and connect a portable battery bank inside the bag to maintain AFU state.
Photograph the wallet balance and then power off the device before bagging.

questions.q: Why is it critical to prevent a seized phone from powering off before forensic examination?
options: A powered-off phone will automatically remote-wipe after 15 minutes.
When the phone enters BFU state, encryption keys are flushed from RAM, making forensic extraction extremely difficult or impossible.
Apple and Google require the device to remain on to honor preservation letters.
A powered-off phone cannot be placed in a Faraday bag without risk of damage.

questions.q: An officer finds a Trezor device during a premises search. The suspect offers to enter the PIN. The officer should:
options: Allow the suspect to unlock it to document the balance on scene.
Decline — the device may have a Duress PIN configured that displays a decoy zero-balance wallet. Seize the device and have the forensics lab handle access.
Ask the suspect to write the PIN on the evidence bag for later reference.
Plug the device into the patrol car computer to verify it is a wallet before deciding whether to seize it.

questions.q: A numbered list of 24 English words is found on a metal plate during a search. The officer's correct handling action is:
options: Photograph the plate, seal it in a tamper-evident evidence bag, and note in the report only that a seed phrase was located and secured.
Read the words aloud and have a partner enter them into CAD notes for documentation.
Type all 24 words verbatim into the incident report to create a complete official record.
Return the item to the suspect as it is not a firearm, controlled substance, or cash equivalent.

questions.q: A Coinbase app is found on a suspect's phone. The correct law enforcement strategy differs from finding MetaMask because:
options: Coinbase holds larger balances and is therefore a higher enforcement priority.
Coinbase is a custodial exchange — a company that holds funds on the user's behalf and is subject to preservation letters, subpoenas, and warrants. MetaMask has no company to serve.
MetaMask is illegal in most jurisdictions; Coinbase is regulated and therefore legal.
Coinbase cannot be subpoenaed without a federal warrant; MetaMask can be subpoenaed at the local level.

questions.q: A Ledger hardware wallet is seized and booked into an evidence locker without a Faraday bag. Two days later, the associated wallet balance has been drained. What risk factor allowed this outcome?
options: The Ledger device transmitted the private key over Bluetooth to the suspect's attorney.
Ledger devices automatically transfer funds to the last connected computer after 48 hours.
The suspect triggered a timer-based wipe that was set before the device was seized.

Without Faraday isolation, the device may have connected to the locker's Wi-Fi, allowing a co-conspirator with the backup seed phrase to drain the funds remotely — or the device itself received commands over wireless.

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios most clearly warrants immediate escalation to federal partners (FBI or HSI)?
options: A local resident lost $8,000 in a Bitcoin ATM scam targeting elderly victims.
A $2 million Pig Butchering loss where suspects are believed to operate from Southeast Asia.
A detective requests tracing software that the local agency cannot afford.
A hardware wallet is seized and the PIN is unknown, requiring forensic extraction.

questions.q: A department's evidence policy defines currency as "coin and paper money" and makes no reference to cryptocurrency. Why is this an operational liability?
options: Federal law mandates that all agency policies must reference cryptocurrency by name.
Officers have no written chain-of-custody standard for digital assets, and a defense attorney can use this gap to argue for evidence suppression.
The policy is automatically invalid under the Bank Secrecy Act once cryptocurrency is involved in a case.
The absence of a digital asset definition means the agency cannot apply for federal grants.

questions.q: The "Two-Person Rule" (Dual Control) in digital asset evidence handling requires two supervisors to be present when:
options: A patrol officer first photographs a suspected seed phrase at a roadside stop.
A digital asset case is filed with the local prosecutor.
A sealed seed phrase is opened or agency-controlled cryptocurrency is transferred to a government wallet.
A preservation letter is sent to a cryptocurrency exchange.

questions.q: The "Kill Chain" in crypto victim intake refers to:
options: The forensic process of tracing funds from one wallet to the next until reaching a VASP.
The 48-hour window following a theft during which freeze requests, exchange preservation letters, and IC3 filings have the greatest chance of success.
The chain of custody required from seizure of a device to forensic examination.
The sequential steps for obtaining a search warrant based on blockchain evidence.

questions.q: A blockchain explorer shows that stolen funds moved from the victim's wallet to a second wallet, and then from that wallet to an address labeled "Binance Hot Wallet." What is the correct next investigative step?
options: Send a preservation letter to Binance requesting that all records related to the identified account be preserved, pending a subpoena for subscriber information.
Arrest the Binance employee whose IP address appears in the WHOIS record.
Post the wallet address to a law enforcement message board and wait for other agencies to identify the account holder.
Contact Tether to freeze the Binance wallet since Binance holds USDT.

questions.q: A student reports that they received a wire transfer from an unknown sender, were instructed to withdraw the cash, and deposit it at a Bitcoin ATM. They believed this was a legitimate remote-work job. This situation is best described as:
options: A legitimate cryptocurrency arbitrage transaction that requires no police action.
A money mule operation — the student was recruited to launder funds for a criminal organization, possibly without full awareness.
A Pig Butchering investment scam in which the student is the primary victim.
A BTM smurfing operation where the student is the primary organizer.

questions.q: Why do criminals prefer to use USDT on the Tron network rather than USDT on Ethereum for high-volume money laundering?
options: Tron USDT transactions are untraceable because Tron does not have a public blockchain.
Tron USDT cannot be frozen by Tether Ltd., whereas Ethereum-based USDT can.
Transaction fees on the Tron network are significantly cheaper and transactions confirm faster than on Ethereum.
The Tron blockchain is regulated by a different agency and is not subject to FinCEN reporting.

questions.q: An officer finds a Bitcoin ATM receipt during a premises search. The most investigatively valuable piece of information on that receipt is:
options: The machine's serial number.
The transaction date, dollar amount, and destination Bitcoin wallet address.
The store name where the BTM is located.
The machine operator's telephone number printed at the bottom.
questions.ref: 2.2 page 1 — Evidence Collection at the Kiosk

questions.q: Which statement about Bitcoin's traceability is accurate and supported by the course material?
options: Bitcoin is pseudonymous — every transaction is public, and linking a person to one address through a subpoena or other means can reveal their entire transaction history.
Bitcoin is fully anonymous — transactions cannot be linked to individuals under any circumstances.
Bitcoin transactions are only visible to law enforcement, not to the public.
Bitcoin becomes untraceable after three wallet-to-wallet hops.

questions.q: A patrol officer tells a Pig Butchering victim: "We will definitely get your money back — the blockchain shows exactly where it went." Why is this statement harmful?
options: The officer should not be speaking to victims — only detectives are authorized to do so.

Tracing where funds went is often possible, but recovery is difficult, expensive, and rare — especially with overseas criminal organizations. The promise sets an expectation that almost certainly cannot be met, damaging the victim's trust and the agency's credibility.
The statement is technically accurate; blockchain tracing guarantees fund recovery.
The statement is harmless because it motivates the victim to cooperate with the investigation.

questions.q: An agency strictly prohibits officers from using personal cryptocurrency wallets to receive, hold, or transfer seized digital assets. This policy primarily protects against:
options: The risk of officers losing their own personal savings in volatile crypto markets.
Compliance with IRS tax reporting requirements for crypto holdings.
The risk of department computers being hacked through officers' personal wallet apps.

The risk of officers misappropriating seized funds — a scenario that has resulted in officer terminations and criminal prosecutions in multiple jurisdictions — and ensures an auditable chain of custody through official agency wallets or approved custodians.
